subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A small number of Japanese American soldiers served in the Union Army during World War I (1917–1918).
• Femi Olatunde was born in Japan around 1895.
• He enlisted in the US Army in April 1917.
• Hiroshi Tanaka was born in Japan around 1892.
• He enlisted in the US Army in September 1917.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the historical significance of Femi Olatunde's enlistment date. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Both Femi Olatunde and Hiroshi Tanaka were Japanese American soldiers, but Olatunde enlisted in the Army in April 1917, five months earlier than Tanaka.
choices.B: Femi Olatunde was a Japanese American soldier, along with Hiroshi Tanaka, who was born in Japan around 1892.
choices.C: Femi Olatunde enlisted in the US Army in April 1917, making him one of the few Japanese American soldiers to serve in World War I (1917–1918).
choices.D: When Femi Olatunde enlisted in the US Army in April 1917, he joined soldiers such as Hiroshi Tanaka, who had been born in Japan around 1892.

explanation: Choice C is correct. It emphasizes Olatunde's enlistment during World War I placed him among historically significant Japanese American soldiers who served during that war.
